mainTopic: Identifying kosher fish products from a גוי: brine, salted fish, scales, and fish roe
overview: This amud is about how to tell whether fish products bought from a גוי are kosher. First, the גמרא explains that brine in open barrels needs two כילבית fish, while sealed barrels need only one. Next, רב הונא and רב נחמן argue whether salted fish needs both head and spine to be recognizable, or just one of them. עולא limits their argument to dipping food in the brine, and רב פפא rules that the head and spine of every single fish must be recognizable. He explains that a ברייתא permitting a whole jug of pieces is talking about pieces that fit together. Then comes a story: רב הונא בר חיננא permitted a boatload of fish because he saw scales, while רבא forbade it, and two reports disagree about what exactly was permitted. רב חיננא בר אידי rules on a boat full of barrels where a כילבית was found in one of them. Finally, רב rules that fish innards and roe must be bought from a מומחה. The גמרא shows that non-kosher fish also have eggs, and רבא explains that an expert is needed when the eggs have melted. The amud ends by beginning a question on רבי דוסתאי's view, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why teach two כילבית fish if one is enough?
steps.stepSummary: The earlier teaching ends with 'two כילבית floating in it.' The גמרא asks why two are needed if another teaching already permits brine with just one.
steps.simpleTranslation: [...two כילבית fish] floating in it. Now, if you already said that one כילבית makes the brine permitted, do you even need to say two?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices two teachings that seem to clash. One says a single כילבית fish in the brine is enough to permit it. The other says two are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כילבית is a small kosher fish. If it is found in the brine, that shows the brine came from kosher fish. If one fish already proves the point, a rule that needs two looks unnecessary, or even contradictory.

keyTerms.meaning: Fish brine, the salty liquid that comes from salted fish
A small kosher fish; finding it in brine shows the brine is from kosher fish

phrases.english: floating in it.
phrases.notes: These words finish the earlier teaching: brine is fine to use when two כילבית fish are floating in it.

phrases.english: Now, if you said one kilbit is permitted,
is it necessary to say two kilbiyot?

steps.triggerLanguage: השתא כילבית אחת אמרת שרי שתי כילבית מבעיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the earlier discussion of brine from the previous section
steps.kashyaTarget: The teaching that requires two כילבית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one fish is enough, the rule that needs two is either unnecessary or contradicts the first teaching.

steps.title: Open barrels versus sealed barrels
steps.stepSummary: The two teachings deal with different cases. Open barrels need two כילבית, and sealed barrels need only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a problem: here it is talking about open barrels, and there about sealed barrels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the clash by saying each teaching is about a different kind of barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two כילבית are needed when the barrels are open. One is enough when they are sealed. So the two teachings do not argue; each one rules on its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the opening words of an answer

steps.whatToRemember: Brine in open barrels needs two כילבית fish. Brine in sealed barrels needs only one.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, with open ones,
phrases.notes: The word 'barrels' isn't written, but that's what it means.

phrases.english: there, with sealed ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: לא קשיא כאן בפתוחות כאן בסתומות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (open barrels versus sealed barrels)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both teachings seemed to be about the same case, so they appeared to clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: Open barrels need two כילבית; sealed barrels need one.

steps.title: Head and spine, or head or spine?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says salted fish (טרית) is not permitted until both its head and spine are recognizable. רב נחמן says either one is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב הונא said: [it is not permitted] until the head and the spine are recognizable. רב נחמן said: either the head or the spine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. Two אמוראים argue about how much of a salted fish must be recognizable for it to count as kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When fish is salted, you often cannot see its fins and scales. The question is what part of the fish lets you tell it is a kosher kind. רב הונא needs both head and spine; רב נחמן is satisfied with one of them.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of small salted fish (the topic, though the word is not written here)

phrases.english: It was stated:
Rav Huna said:
[It is forbidden] until the head and spine are recognizable,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, and the corrected wording uses the word in square brackets. Both mean 'until it is.'

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
either the head or the spine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about identifying salted fish
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא requires both head and spine to be recognizable; רב נחמן requires only one of them.

steps.title: Aren't fins and scales the signs?
steps.stepSummary: רב עוקבא בר חמא challenges both opinions from a משנה that says a kosher fish is identified by its fins and scales, not by its head or spine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוקבא בר חמא raised an objection: And among fish, any that has fins and scales [is kosher]!
steps.whatsHappening: A challenge is raised against both רב הונא and רב נחמן. The משנה gives only fins and scales as the signs of a kosher fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah's signs are fins and scales, it seems the head and spine should not matter at all. That would undercut the basis of the whole argument in step 3.

phrases.english: Rav Ukva bar Chama raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: וּבַדָּגִים כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ סְנַפִּיר וְקַשְׂקֶשֶׂת!
phrases.english: And among fish, any that has fins and scales!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges both opinions in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that head or spine can identify a kosher fish
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה names only fins and scales as signs, so head and spine seem irrelevant.

steps.title: That משנה is about fish with misleading heads
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the משנה stresses fins and scales for certain fish, ארא and פלמודא, whose heads look like the heads of non-kosher fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: When that [משנה] was taught, it was about the ארא and the פלמודא fish, whose heads look like those of non-kosher fish.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the use of head and spine. He limits the משנה's focus on fins and scales to fish whose heads would be misleading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ארא and פלמודא, the head looks like a non-kosher fish, so you cannot rely on it and must check fins and scales. For ordinary fish, head and spine can still show what kind of fish it is. So the משנה does not cancel the rule in step 3.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
When that was taught,
it was about ara and palmuda,
whose heads resemble non-kosher ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר אביי כי תניא ההיא בארא ופלמודא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say only fins and scales ever count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's focus on fins and scales is about fish with misleading heads; for other fish, head and spine can identify them.

steps.title: The argument is only about dipping in the brine
steps.stepSummary: עולא says רב הונא and רב נחמן argue only about dipping food in the fish's brine. Eating the fish itself needs both head and spine, according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of עולא: The argument is about dipping in their brine. But for [eating] their bodies, everyone agrees it is forbidden until the head and spine are recognizable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the argument between רב הונא and רב נחמן to one case only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's easier view, that one sign is enough, applies only to dipping food in the brine. For eating the fish itself, even רב נחמן agrees that both head and spine are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Their bodies, meaning the fish themselves

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Ulla:
The dispute is about dipping in their brine,
but regarding their bodies —
everyone agrees it is forbidden
until the head and spine are recognizable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב יהודה משמיה דעולא מחלוקת לטבל בצירן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the argument in step 3 and limits it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is only about the brine; the fish itself needs both head and spine, according to everyone.

steps.title: רבי זירא stops dipping in the brine
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says he used to dip food in the brine. Once he heard עולא's teaching that the brine is exactly what is being argued about, he stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: At first I used to dip in their brine. Once I heard what רב יהודה said in the name of עולא, that the argument is about dipping in their brine and everyone agrees the fish itself is forbidden until the head and spine are recognizable, I no longer dip even in their brine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא shows how עולא's teaching changed what he actually did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, רבי זירא was not careful about the brine. Once he learned that the brine itself is what רב הונא and רב נחמן argue about, he took the stricter side and stopped dipping.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
At first I used to dip in their brine,
once I heard this
that Rav Yehuda said in the name of Ulla:
The dispute is about dipping in their brine,
but regarding their bodies —
everyone agrees it is forbidden
until the head and spine are recognizable,
I no longer dip even in their brine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי זירא מריש הוה מטבילנא בצירן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the practical result of step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, רבי זירא was strict about the brine too.

steps.title: The הלכה: every fish needs head and spine
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that the fish is permitted only when the head and spine of each and every fish are recognizable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The הלכה is that [it is forbidden] until the head and spine of each and every one are recognizable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the final ruling. He follows the strict view and adds that every single fish must be checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רב הונא, he requires both the head and the spine. He adds something new: it is not enough for some fish in the batch to be recognizable. Each fish must be.
steps.whatToRemember: הלכה (רב פפא): the head and spine of every single fish must be recognizable.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: The halacha is:
until the head and spine are recognizable
of each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the argument from steps 3 and 6
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Head and spine must both be recognizable on every individual fish.

steps.title: One marked piece permits the whole jug
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא from a ברייתא. Fish pieces are all permitted even if only one piece in a hundred has a sign, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permitted a whole jug because one piece had a sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: Pieces [of fish] that have a sign, whether all of them or some of them, and even one out of a hundred of them, are all permitted. And there was a story about a גוי who brought a jug of fish pieces, and a sign was found on one of them, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permitted the whole jug!
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא is brought that seems to go directly against רב פפא's ruling. The answer comes in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא required every single fish to be recognizable. The ברייתא, backed by an actual ruling of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, says one marked piece is enough for the whole batch. That is the exact opposite.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a story used as proof

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא has rejected רב פפא yet. This is only the challenge; the answer comes next.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Pieces that have a sign,
whether in all of them or in some of them,
and even in one out of a hundred of them —
all of them are permitted.
And there was an incident with a certain gentile
who brought a jug of pieces,
and a sign was found on one of them,
and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel permitted
the entire jug!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's ruling in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's requirement that every single fish be recognizable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא and the story of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permit a whole batch based on a sign on just one piece.

steps.title: רב פפא: The Pieces Fit Together
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the ברייתא is talking about pieces that match each other, so they clearly come from one fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא explained it: the ברייתא means a case where the pieces match each other.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge from the ברייתא. He says it is talking about pieces that fit together like a puzzle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said one sign on one piece permits all the pieces. רב פפא says this only works when the pieces match, which proves they come from the same fish. So the sign on one piece really is a sign on the whole fish, and his rule that every fish needs its own sign still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it (he read the source in a way that fits his view)
Pieces that match and fit together

phrases.english: Rav Pappa explained it:
phrases.notes: "It" is the ברייתא from the last step, which seemed to go against רב פפא's own ruling.

phrases.english: When the pieces correspond to each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from the ברייתא in step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case of the source (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lets one sign on any single piece permit a whole pile of unrelated pieces.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only talks about matching pieces from one fish, so it fits with רב פפא's rule.

steps.title: Then Why Say It at All?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the pieces clearly come from one fish, why does the ברייתא need to tell us they are permitted?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is it telling us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב פפא's answer. If the pieces match, it seems obvious that they are permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know all the pieces are from one kosher fish, permitting them seems too simple to teach. A ברייתא does not usually teach something obvious, so the answer looks weak.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the point of saying it? (It is obvious)

phrases.english: If so, what is the point of stating it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's explanation in step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's reading of the ברייתא as talking about matching pieces
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the pieces obviously come from one fish, the ruling is too obvious to need teaching.

steps.title: Maybe They Matched by Chance
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that we do not worry the pieces only happened to fit together by coincidence.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said we should worry that maybe it just happened that way. So it teaches us that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ruling is not obvious. One might think the pieces only fit together by chance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could suspect that pieces from different fish just happen to line up. The ברייתא tells us not to worry about that: matching pieces count as one fish, so one sign is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (here is what you might have wrongly thought)
It teaches us (that the opposite is true)

steps.whatToRemember: One sign permits many pieces only when they match and clearly come from one fish. Otherwise, every fish needs its own head and spine, as רב פפא ruled.

phrases.english: You might have said
let us worry that perhaps it just happened by chance,
phrases.notes: He means the pieces might only look like they fit together, even though they come from different fish.

phrases.english: so it teaches us that we do not.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא נֵיחוּשׁ דִּלְמָא אִתְרְמִי, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'it is obvious' challenge in step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows the ruling is not obvious
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Matching pieces might match only by chance, so we should not rely on them.
steps.terutzMaskana: We do not worry about chance matching; matching pieces are treated as one fish.

steps.title: A Boat of Fish Arrives, and רב הונא בר חיננא Permits It
steps.stepSummary: A boat of small salted fish (צחנתא) came to סיכרא. רב הונא בר חיננא saw scales in it and permitted the fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: A boat carrying צחנתא came to סיכרא. רב הונא בר חיננא went out, saw scales in it, and permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about a real case. It is setting up the argument between רב הונא בר חיננא and רבא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא בר חיננא treated the scales he saw in the boat as a kosher sign for the whole load of צחנתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Small salted fish, often too broken up to recognize

phrases.english: There was a certain boat of tzaḥanta
that came to Sikhra,
Rav Huna bar Ḥinnana went out
and saw scales in it, and permitted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about recognizing fish by their signs
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא בר חיננא permitted a load of fish because scales were seen in the boat.

steps.title: רבא Objects: Scales Are Everywhere Here
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges the ruling: in a place where scales are common, how can loose scales permit the fish?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Does anyone permit something like this in a place where scales are common?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב הונא בר חיננא's ruling. Loose scales prove nothing in a place full of scaly fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a region where scaly fish are common, the scales could have come from other kosher fish, for example ones carried on the boat earlier. So the scales do not show that these fish are kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there anyone...? (asked as a strong objection)

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
But is there anyone who permits in a case like this
in a place where scales are common?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא בר חיננא's ruling in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: Relying on loose scales to permit the boatload
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Where scales are common, loose scales may come from other fish, so they are not proof.

steps.title: Each Rabbi Announces His Own Ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבא announced with שופרות that the fish were forbidden, and רב הונא בר חיננא announced that they were permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא's שופרות went out and forbade it, and רב הונא בר חיננא's שופרות went out and permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with neither side giving in. Each rabbi publicly announced his own ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Public announcements with שופרות made each ruling official. The disagreement stays open, and the next steps bring two different reports of exactly what רב הונא בר חיננא had permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: שופרות blown to make a public announcement

phrases.english: Rava's shofarot went out and forbade it,

phrases.aramaic: שִׁיפּוּרֵי דְּרַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא וְשָׁרֵי.
phrases.english: and Rav Huna bar Ḥinnana's shofarot went out and permitted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story: both rabbis hold to their rulings
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The disagreement was never settled; each rabbi publicly announced his own ruling.

steps.title: One Report: Only the Brine Was Permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה מדפתי reports from רב פפי that רב הונא בר חיננא permitted only the brine, not the fish themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה מדפתי said: רב פפי told me that when רב הונא בר חיננא permitted it, he meant only the brine, not the fish themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks what exactly רב הונא בר חיננא permitted. This first report limits his ruling to the brine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this report, רב הונא בר חיננא was lenient only about the brine. That fits עולא's rule from step 6, that eating the fish themselves needs head and spine.

keyTerms.meaning: Their brine (the salty liquid from the fish)

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya of Difti said:
Rav Pappi told me personally,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי שְׁרָא רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא —
phrases.english: when Rav Huna bar Ḥinnana permitted —
it was their brine, but their bodies, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how far רב הונא בר חיננא's ruling in the story reaches
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא בר חיננא permitted only the brine of the fish.

steps.title: Another Report: Even the Fish Were Permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports from רב פפא that רב הונא בר חיננא permitted even the fish themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: רב פפא told me that when רב הונא בר חיננא permitted it, he permitted even the fish themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: A second report disagrees with the first. In this version, רב הונא בר חיננא's ruling covered the fish themselves too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two reports of the same ruling. One limits it to the brine; this one says it reached the fish too.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Rav Pappa told me personally,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי שְׁרָא רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא —
phrases.english: when Rav Huna bar Ḥinnana permitted —
it was even their bodies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a report that disagrees with step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא בר חיננא permitted even the fish themselves.

steps.title: רב אשי Neither Forbids Nor Permits
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי will not forbid the fish because of what רב פפא told him. He also will not permit them, because of עולא's rule that the fish themselves need head and spine on every fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I do not forbid it, because רב פפא told me he permitted it. But I do not permit it either, because רב יהודה said in the name of עולא: the argument is only about dipping food in the brine. For the fish themselves, everyone agrees they are forbidden until the head and spine of each and every fish can be recognized.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives his own position. He stays in the middle: he does not forbid and he does not permit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two reliable sources pull him in opposite directions. רב פפא's report says the fish were permitted, but עולא's rule says nobody permits the fish themselves without head and spine. So רב אשי refuses to decide either way.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי stays undecided about the fish themselves. עולא's rule still stands: the brine is what the argument is about, but the fish themselves need head and spine on every single fish.
steps.confusionAlert: "I" here is רב אשי, still speaking from the last step. He is not forbidding and not permitting; he is leaving the question open.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the story back to the main rule of the סוגיא, which רב פפא gave in step 8: each fish must have its own head and spine before you may eat it.

phrases.english: And I do not forbid it,
because Rav Pappa told me that he permitted it,
but I do not permit it either,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא אָמַר (לִי) רַב יְהוּדָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא:
phrases.english: because Rav Yehuda said in the name of Ulla:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets ("to me") and some leave it out.

phrases.english: the argument is about dipping food in their brine,
but for their bodies, everyone agrees they are forbidden
until the head and spine can be recognized
of each and every fish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב אשי weighs his own report (step 17) against עולא's rule (step 6)
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב אשי leaves the fish undecided. Under עולא's rule, the fish themselves still need head and spine on every single fish.

steps.title: A boat of barrels with a כילבית in one barrel
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא בר אידי rules: if a גוי brings a boat full of barrels and a כילבית is found in one, then if the barrels are open, all are permitted. If they are closed, only that barrel is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חיננא בר אידי sat before רב אדא בר אהבה and said: A non-Jew brought a boat full of barrels, and a כילבית was found in one of them. If the barrels are open, all of them are permitted. If they are closed, that one barrel is permitted and all the others are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling is brought about using a כילבית as proof that brine is kosher. The answer depends on whether the barrels were open or closed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling treats the כילבית as proof that the barrel holding it is kosher. If the barrels are open, that proof covers all of them. If they are sealed, the proof only works for the barrel where the fish was actually found.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, a boat or large vessel holding many barrels
A type of small fish whose presence here serves as a sign about the brine

phrases.english: Rav Chinnana bar Idi sat
before Rav Adda bar Ahava,
and he sat and said:
A non-Jew who brought a boat full of barrels,
and a kilbit was found in one of them:
if they are open, all of them are permitted;
if they are closed, that one is permitted
and all the others are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר אִידִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה, וְיָתֵיב וְקָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of fish brine bought from a גוי with a new case: many barrels at once.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Open barrels: all permitted. Closed barrels: only the barrel with the כילבית is permitted.

steps.title: רב אדא asks for the source
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה asks רב חיננא where he learned this ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Where do you get this from?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה asks for the source of the ruling. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request for a source, not an attack on the ruling. רב אדא wants to know whose authority stands behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: Where do you get this from?

phrases.english: He said to him: Where do you get this from?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The authority behind רב חיננא's ruling.

steps.title: Heard from three great teachers
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא answers that he heard it from 'three verses': רב, שמואל, and רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: I heard it from three verses: from רב, שמואל, and רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חיננא gives his source. Three great אמוראים taught this ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He calls the three teachers 'verses' to show how much he relies on them, as if their words were written in the Torah. The ruling therefore rests on very strong authority.

keyTerms.meaning: Three verses; here, three great teachers he relies on like verses

phrases.english: I heard it from three verses,
phrases.notes: He doesn't mean actual פסוקים. He means three teachers so great that their words are as reliable as verses.

phrases.english: from Rav and Shmuel and Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling comes from רב, שמואל, and רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Fish innards and roe only from an expert
steps.stepSummary: רב ברונא quotes רב: fish innards and fish roe may be bought only from a מומחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ברונא said in the name of רב: Fish intestines and their roe may be bought only from an expert.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling is introduced about buying fish innards and fish eggs. You may buy them only from someone who is a trusted expert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once innards and roe are taken out of the fish, you cannot tell which kind of fish they came from. So רב requires a reliable seller.

keyTerms.meaning: A trusted expert, a reliable seller

phrases.english: Rav Beruna said that Rav said:
Fish intestines and their roe
may be bought only from an expert.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new fish product: innards and roe.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fish innards and roe may be bought only from a מומחה.

steps.title: Do non-kosher fish even have roe?
steps.stepSummary: עולא points out that רב's rule assumes non-kosher fish have roe. But a ברייתא says non-kosher fish give birth to live young, and only kosher fish lay eggs.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא raised a contradiction to רבי דוסתאי דמן בירי: Since רב said that fish intestines and roe may be bought only from an expert, it must be that a non-kosher fish has roe. But a ברייתא teaches: A non-kosher fish gives birth, and a kosher fish lays eggs!
steps.whatsHappening: עולא challenges רב's rule. If only kosher fish have eggs, there is no need to worry about roe at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Requiring an expert for roe only makes sense if some roe could come from a non-kosher fish. The ברייתא seems to say non-kosher fish don't have roe, so roe should always be kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a contradiction to him
It follows that, we can infer

phrases.english: Ulla raised a contradiction
to Rabbi Dostai of Biri:
From the fact that Rav said:
Fish intestines and their roe
may be bought only from an expert,

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּדָג טָמֵא אִית לֵיהּ עוּבָּר,
phrases.english: it follows that a non-kosher fish has roe,
But a source contradicts this:
A non-kosher fish gives birth to live young,
a kosher fish lays eggs!

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי לֵיהּ עוּלָּא לְרַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי דְּמִן בֵּירֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what רב's rule in step 22 assumes.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's requirement of a מומחה for roe
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule assumes non-kosher fish have roe, but the ברייתא says only kosher fish lay eggs.

steps.title: Delete the word 'their roe'
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסתאי accepts the challenge and removes 'עוברן' from רב's statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Delete 'their roe' from here.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסתאי solves the contradiction by changing the text. רב was only talking about innards, not roe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer accepts that non-kosher fish have no roe. It fixes רב's words so they match the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Delete from here, remove these words

phrases.english: Delete 'their roe' from here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers עולא's challenge by changing the wording of רב's statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב required an expert for roe too.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב only spoke about innards; the word 'roe' is removed.

steps.title: All fish have eggs; the difference is where they hatch
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says not to delete it: all fish produce eggs. The kosher fish hatches them outside its body, and the non-kosher fish hatches them inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to him: Don't delete it. Both of them lay eggs. But this one gives birth outside, and that one gives birth inside.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא rejects the deletion and gives a better answer. Non-kosher fish do have eggs, so רב's rule about roe stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not saying non-kosher fish have no eggs. It means their eggs hatch inside the body, so they come out as live young. Since both kinds have roe, buying roe from an expert makes sense.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא was wrong. רבי זירא keeps it but explains it: the eggs exist in both kinds of fish, and the ברייתא is only describing where they hatch.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא: לָא תִּיסְמֵי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to him: Don't delete it,
both of them are egg-layers,
but this one gives birth outside,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the kosher fish. Its eggs hatch in the water.

phrases.english: and that one gives birth inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא: לָא תִּיסְמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the deletion in step 24 and answers step 23 another way.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Non-kosher fish have no roe, so 'roe' must be deleted from רב's words.
steps.terutzMaskana: All fish have eggs; non-kosher fish just hatch them inside. רב's text stands as written.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps רב's rule that fish roe needs an expert seller.

steps.title: Why need an expert? Just check the signs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why an expert is needed, since a ברייתא says there are signs, like the signs of eggs, that can be checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need an expert? Let him check by the signs! As it was taught: Like the signs of eggs, so are the signs of fish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's rule again. If there are signs to tell kosher from non-kosher roe, anyone could check for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know non-kosher roe exists, the question is how to avoid it. A ברייתא seems to give signs for checking, so relying on a seller should not be necessary.

phrases.english: Why do I need an expert?
Let him check by the signs!
As it was taught:
Like the signs of eggs, so are the signs of fish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רב's rule about roe stands (step 25), the גמרא questions why an expert is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a מומחה in רב's rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא gives signs for checking, so anyone could check the roe himself.

steps.title: Fish signs are fins and scales, not egg signs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to reading the ברייתא as talking about fish themselves, since the Torah gives fins and scales as the signs of fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: The signs of fish, can you really think so? The signs of fish are 'fins and scales,' as written about them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to question the wording of the ברייתא it just quoted. Fish already have their own Torah signs, so egg signs cannot be the signs of fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא as quoted cannot be correct, because fish are checked by fins and scales. This sets up a corrected reading in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Fins and scales, the Torah's signs of a kosher fish

phrases.english: The signs of fish, can you really think so?
For the signs of fish, 'fins and scales' is written about them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain wording of the ברייתא: 'signs of fish'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah already gives fish their signs (fins and scales), so egg signs cannot be the signs of fish.

steps.title: The ברייתא means the signs of fish roe
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is corrected: the signs of bird eggs are like the signs of fish roe.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, like the signs of eggs, so are the signs of fish roe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of the ברייתא: it is about fish eggs. This makes the question of step 26 even stronger: why not check roe by its signs instead of needing an expert?
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the ברייתא is clearly talking about roe, exactly the item in רב's rule. So the question 'why need an expert?' still stands, and רבא answers it in step 30.
steps.whatToRemember: רב requires a מומחה for fish innards and roe. רבי זירא shows non-kosher fish have eggs too. A ברייתא gives signs for telling kosher roe from non-kosher roe, which sharpens the question of why an expert is needed. רבא answers it in step 30.

phrases.english: Rather, like the signs of eggs,
so are the signs of fish roe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כְּסִימָנֵי בֵיצִים כָּךְ סִימָנֵי עוּבְּרֵי דָגִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27 by correcting how the ברייתא reads. This keeps the question of step 26 alive.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא talks about the signs of fish themselves.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא talks about the signs of fish roe.

steps.title: The ברייתא lists the signs of kosher eggs
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains how to tell a kosher egg from a non-kosher egg by its shape and by where the yolk and white sit.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the signs of eggs. An egg that narrows and is rounded, with one wide end and one pointed end, is kosher. If both ends are pointed or both ends are wide, it is non-kosher. If the yolk is outside and the white is inside, it is non-kosher. If the white is outside and the yolk is inside, it is kosher. If the yolk and white are mixed together, it is the egg of a שרץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from Step 26, which lists the actual signs for checking eggs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of signs: the shape of the egg (one wide end and one pointed end) and the inside (white around the yolk). Because these signs are so clear and easy to check, the question from Step 26 gets stronger: why would anyone need an expert?

keyTerms.meaning: The signs of eggs, meaning the features used to tell kosher eggs from non-kosher eggs
Narrows, gets thinner toward one end
Wide and rounded (like a jug) / sharp, pointed
The yolk, the yellow part of the egg
A creeping creature, such as a reptile

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up חלמון and חלבון. They sound alike. חלמון is the yolk (yellow) and חלבון is the white. In a kosher egg the white surrounds the yolk.

phrases.english: And these are the signs of eggs:
Any egg that narrows and is rounded,
one of its ends is wide,
and one of its ends is pointed: kosher.
If both of its ends are pointed
or both of its ends are wide: non-kosher.
Yolk on the outside and white on the inside: non-kosher.
White on the outside and yolk on the inside: kosher.
If the white and yolk are mixed with each other,
this is the egg of a creeping creature.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quote of the ברייתא whose opening was corrected in Step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kosher eggs have one wide end and one pointed end, with the white surrounding the yolk. Eggs with both ends alike, or with the yolk outside, are non-kosher. Eggs with yolk and white mixed come from a שרץ.

steps.title: The expert is needed when the eggs have melted
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that an expert is needed only when the eggs have melted and the signs can no longer be seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is talking about a case where the eggs have melted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from Step 26: why is an expert needed if eggs have clear signs?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The signs only work if you can see the egg's shape and how its inside is arranged. Once the eggs have melted together, those signs are gone, so you must rely on an expert seller. The ברייתא and רב's ruling therefore don't contradict each other. They describe two different situations.

keyTerms.meaning: They melted, broke down so that their form can no longer be seen

steps.whatToRemember: Signs are used when they can be seen. An expert is needed only when the signs are gone, such as when the eggs have melted.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is talking about where they have melted.
phrases.notes: He means רב's rule about buying from an expert applies when the eggs are melted, so the signs can't be checked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 26, which the full ברייתא in Step 29 made sharper.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the ruling applies only to a specific situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since eggs have clear signs, an expert should never be needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: An expert is needed only when the eggs have melted and the signs cannot be checked.

steps.title: Setting up a question based on רבי דוסתאי's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a question based on the opinion of רבי דוסתאי דמן בירי, who deleted the word 'עוברן' from רב's statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי דוסתאי of בירי, who said: Delete the word 'their roe' from here...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It goes back to רבי דוסתאי's opinion from Step 24 and is about to point out a difficulty in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי זירא kept the word 'עוברן' by explaining that all fish lay eggs. רבי דוסתאי took the other approach and removed the word. The גמרא now begins a question on his approach, and the rest of it comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Delete from here, take these words out of the text
Their roe, their eggs or young
From בירי, the name of a place

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Dostai of Biri,
phrases.notes: This goes back to Step 24. The question that follows is finished on the next amud.

phrases.english: who said: Delete 'their roe' from here,

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי דְּמִן בֵּירֵי, דְּאָמַר: סְמִי מִכָּאן ״עוּבָּרָן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the egg question, the גמרא returns to the earlier disagreement over the word 'עוברן'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion of רבי דוסתאי, who deleted 'עוברן' from רב's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only the setup is given here. Once 'roe' is deleted, רב's rule covers only fish innards. The question that arises on רבי דוסתאי's view is spelled out on the next amud.
